_comment: The Tourist voice (NPCConversation II.1b, SpeciesVoice). speech: the rules run over any shared line they say. voice: openers and closers. thought: their own thoughts by situation. script: two-person scripts, speaker 0 is always the Tourist.

openers: As they say on the television,
Forgive me, I am still learning your idioms, but
In the words of the weatherman,
Hold still one moment... there. So:
My cousin on the home sphere will not believe this, but
Page forty-one of the phrasebook says:
We interrupt this programme to say:
If I have understood correctly, and I rarely have,
Thirty-nine light years I travelled to hear this, and
As your famous quiz host would say,
Truly, the cat is out of the pyjamas:
With the greatest respect for your species,
How do you say... ah yes:
I have seen this on the documentary!
The Analyzers would open this up to check, but
One more photograph and then I listen. Click. So,
I write this down for the album:
It is the bee's elbows, but
My translator box is warm, but here goes:
I was told by a very kind bus driver that
Ah! A local custom, I think:
The guidebook is unclear here, so
Speaking as a big fan of humanity,
One moment, the flash is charging. Right:
closers: Back to you in the studio.
I have it on film now.
That is a wrap, as you say.
My cousin will be so jealous.
We will be right back after these messages.
Please do not change the channel.
Goodnight, and good luck with the weather.
Ten out of ten, would visit again.
I have made a note of it.
Like on television, but in colour.
What a time to be visiting!
The flash was on, do not worry.
See you in the next episode.
That one is for the postcard.
I have rewound it in my head already.
Thank you for your patience with a visitor.
I will explain it to my sphere.

generic: I took {thirty-six|twenty-four|twelve} photographs of a bus stop today. All of them excellent.
The man at the kiosk said 'cheers, love'. I have written it down to study.
Why do humans say 'fine' when they are not fine? Another mystery for the album.
I queued for twenty minutes and did not know what for. It was a lovely queue.
A pigeon looked at me. I looked at the pigeon. We are both visitors here.
My film roll is nearly finished. {Thirty-five|Thirty-four|Thirty-three} down, so few to go.
I tried to fold a road map. The road map won.
Somebody held a door open for me. I held it back for them. We were there for some time.
The soap opera ended on a cliff. I must know if Rosalind survives the cliff.
Humans put milk in tea, then argue about it. I adore them.
I bought a souvenir {snow globe|keyring|tea towel}. It has a picture of this exact street.
The toaster made the bread black again. Gravity I can bend. Bread, no.
A child waved at me from a bus. I waved for eleven minutes after it left.
I watched the weather forecast twice. Both times it rained on the map only.
How do they know which coin is which? The faces are all so serious.
I said 'break a leg' to a waiter. He did not understand. Neither, I think, did I.
Today I learned the word 'drizzle'. Very useful. It is drizzling now.
The advert said 'new and improved'. I bought both, to compare.
My camera strap broke. I am holding it like an egg now.
Humans whistle when they are happy. I tried. It came out as a frequency.
A sign said 'Do not feed the ducks'. I apologised to the ducks.
I have {four|seven|nine} postcards and nobody at home has a letterbox.
The laundrette is a temple. Round windows, warm air, everyone waiting quietly.
The man on the bench is asleep. I will photograph him gently. Without flash.
I keep the receipts. Every one. Small paper diaries of what humans sell.
Humans say 'it is raining cats and dogs'. I looked up. Disappointed again.
The quiz show asked the capital of a country I flew over. I still got it wrong.
I {hummed|sang|whistled} the theme tune of the evening news. A stranger joined in.
Someone called me 'mate'. I am now a mate. I must tell the sphere.
A small dog barked at me. Fair. I am very unusual from down there.
I bought a tourist hat that says 'I love' and then a heart. I do. I really do.
The video shop man recommended a film about aliens. It was quite rude about us.
I tried chewing gum. Where does it go? Nobody will tell me.
Humans shake hands to say hello. I shook {three|five|six} hands before breakfast.
A street musician played only for me. I paid with a photograph. He seemed confused.
I can cross a galaxy in an afternoon and I cannot work this ticket machine.
The newspaper has a crossword. I have filled it with what I wished the answers were.
People here argue about football like it is a religion. I am taking notes.
The shop lady asked if I wanted a bag. I wanted three. They were free!
My guidebook says this café is 'charming'. It is. The guidebook is never wrong.
A human told me I have 'a face for radio'. I think it was a compliment about radio.
I sat on a park bench for an hour, as humans do. Nothing happened. It was perfect.
Someone sneezed and everyone said 'bless you'. I said it late. Very late.
I bought a disposable camera to dispose of. I could not. It was too beautiful.
Humans keep their best plates for guests and eat off the chipped ones. So noble.
I have learned to say 'sorry' first in any situation. It works about half the time.
The lift played music between floors. Who composes for lifts? I want to meet them.
I tried to tip the bus driver. He laughed. I photographed the laugh.
The television told me to 'not try this at home'. So I am trying it here.
I think the chemist developed my film upside down. Or this town is.
Humans smell of soap and bread and worry. It is my favourite smell in the galaxy.
There is a sale at the {shoe shop|chemist|record shop}. I do not need anything. I must go.
The clock tower is three minutes slow. Should I fix it? No. I would only break it.
I keep a list of human greetings. 'Alright?' is my favourite. It asks and answers.
A woman asked me where the station was. Me! I felt so local.
I watched a man parallel park. Real gravity manipulation. Pure skill.
The cat in the window has ignored me for a week. I respect it enormously.
I tried to buy a single grape. The grocer gave me the whole bunch. Humans!
They play the same song on every radio this month. I know all the words. All of them.
Humans call it 'small talk'. To me it is the biggest talk there is.
I put a coin in the fountain and wished for more coins. Is that allowed?
The kebab man knows my order now. I have never been so honoured.
Someone wrote 'wash me' on a dirty van. A poet. This planet is full of poets.
My sunglasses are for style. I do not have the eyes for them. Style is enough.
I stood on the wrong side of the escalator. A man explained. I thanked him for an hour.
I measured the bus stop with my eyes. Two metres and some hope.
My phrasebook says 'where is the lavatory' on every page. A busy planet.
Somebody played a guitar badly in the square. It was the best concert of my life.
I have learned {two|three|four} new swear words. I will not use them. I will treasure them.
A human asked if I was 'one of those Greys'. I said I am a Tourist. We both nodded.
The vending machine kept my coin. A tax for visitors, I think. Fair.
I am getting the hang of the umbrella. Mostly the hang. Not yet the opening.
Humans write their names on their lunch in the office fridge. Such trust, such fear.
The postman whistled at the dog and the dog whistled back. No. I imagined that.
I asked a policeman the time. He told me. Then he asked mine. Lovely man.
The tram rattled through a time loop warning sign at a gentle forty. So careful, humans.
I photographed a puddle. It had the whole sky in it. Two for one.
The cinema sells sweets louder than the film. I bought the loudest ones.
A grandmother gave me a biscuit for no reason. Earth, you are too much.
I do not understand money, but I understand change. It jingles. Good.

sleep: My eyes are so heavy. Heavier than a neutron star, and I have lifted one.
Humans sleep a third of their lives. I finally understand why. Bed.
I fell asleep during the {late film|test card|shipping forecast}. Best sleep of my life.
Yawning is contagious. I have caught it from the whole tram.
Thirty-nine light years of jet lag. It all arrives at once, around now.
I am so tired I photographed my own feet. Twice. By accident.
A hotel pillow. Flat as a pancake, as you say. I will love it anyway.
I must sleep or I will start agreeing with the Analyzers.
Counting sheep. I have reached {two hundred|four hundred|nine hundred}. The sheep are tired too.
The television says 'goodnight' at closedown. I obey the television.
My big head is nodding. It is very far to nod with a head this big.
Sleep, then more sightseeing. The sights will still be there. Probably.
Even my camera battery is flat. We will both recharge tonight.
I lay down for one minute and woke in a different {hour|day|channel}.
Humans say 'sleep tight'. I will try. I do not know how tight.
hunger: My stomach is making the noise of a ship entering orbit.
I could eat a horse, as humans say. I will not. I will eat a sandwich.
Food on Earth comes in so many shapes! I want to eat {a triangle|a spiral|a cube}.
I tried to cook. The smoke alarm reviewed it. One star.
Hungry. The chip shop is calling. Its voice is vinegar.
Our food at home is a grey paste. Your worst sandwich is a feast.
I skipped lunch to photograph lunch. A mistake.
Is a hot dog a dog? I must eat one to find out.
The bakery smells like happiness. I will buy {one|two|six} of everything.
My tummy rumbles. The humans nearby think it is thunder.
I am so hungry I could eat the guidebook. It has pictures of food.
Breakfast is the most important meal, says the cereal box. I believe the box.
Spaghetti. A meal you must wind up like a cable. Brilliant engineering.
A pie. I want a pie. I do not know what is inside. That is the adventure.
Food first, then the museum. A wise human said that. Maybe me.
work: Back to the survey. Somebody must count the lampposts of this town.
The embassy wants a report on {doorbells|traffic cones|post boxes}. I have so many photos.
My shift starts soon. I am the only one there who can lift the shelves without hands.
A job! Humans pay you to be useful. And I get a little badge.
My manager says 'teamwork makes the dream work'. I will put it on the monument.
I fill in a timesheet every day. Even time, humans write down. Wonderful.
Today I must catalogue {forty|sixty|ninety} postcards for the home archive.
I work at the gravity desk. Nobody comes to the gravity desk. I read magazines.
Work. Then lunch. Then work. Humans built a rhythm, and I dance to it.
The photocopier jammed again. I can fold space but not that paper.
My colleague brings cake on Fridays. I would work here for free. Do not tell them.
I must finish the tram timetables before the Warpers fold the route again.
Clocking in. The little machine goes 'chunk'. My favourite sound of the day.
My boss said 'think outside the box'. Which box? I have been looking all week.
Overtime again. More hours, more euros, more postcards.
leisure: A free afternoon! I shall watch {the snooker|a game show|the cookery programme} with full attention.
I want to do nothing, the way humans do nothing. It is harder than it looks.
A day off. I will go to the museum and photograph people looking at paintings.
The arcade! Many lights, many noises. I will lose all my tokens with joy.
Feet up, telly on, as they say. My feet do not go up far. It counts.
I have rented {three|five|eight} videotapes. The weekend is spoken for.
Bored. Wonderful. On Zeta nobody is allowed to be bored for long.
I need fun. Perhaps bingo. The humans shout when they win. I want to shout.
A picnic! I will sit on a blanket and be eaten by ants, like a local.
The cinema has a matinee. I will sit in the front row and see everything enormous.
Today I will sightsee the sights I have already sighted. Again, slower.
A jigsaw of a lighthouse. One thousand pieces. All of them sky.
I want to dance at a disco. The lights go round and round, like home.
Let me feed the ducks. The sign at the other pond said no. This pond did not say.
I deserve a day of television. All of it. Even the adverts.
crime: That postcard rack is unguarded... No. Tourists pay. It says so in the book.
I could lift that {wallet|handbag|car} with gravity alone. I will lift my hat to it instead.
The souvenir is so small and the shop so busy. I put it back. Twice.
Stealing is a human tradition on television. But not in real life, I think.
An Analyzer would just take the parking meter apart. I am not an Analyzer.
The goddess with the bounties is always watching. I read about it. I behave.
I want that road sign for the monument. Perhaps I could ask the council.
Nobody is watching the fruit stall. I paid anyway and left a photo as a tip.
On the detective shows the thief always gets caught. Good. Very good. I will not.
A lost {umbrella|glove|scarf} on the bench. Is it free? I will hand it in, to be safe.
I teleported a pen from the bank by accident. I must teleport it back.
My fingers are itchy for that hotel ashtray. Humans say every guest takes one.
The cash register is open. So many coins with faces. No. Eyes forward.
Shoplifting, the poster says, is a crime. I did not know the word. Now I avoid it.
I could fold this shop into my pocket. That would be rude. Also illegal.
hygiene: I smell of fried onions and film developer. Time for the shower.
My big head is dusty. A big head collects a lot of dust.
Bubble bath! The bottle promised 'a spa experience'. I want the experience.
I must wash before I meet more humans. They notice. They are polite about it.
The rain washed me halfway. I will finish the job with {soap|shampoo|bath salts}.
Deodorant. Humans spray themselves like plants. I will try the pine one.
Hot water from a tap, any time you want. And humans complain about it!
A pigeon was not polite to my shoulder. A wash is needed.
My ship has a sterilising field. Your soap smells better.
I wore the same tourist shirt for {three|four|five} days. It is time to let it rest.
I am sticky from the ice cream. Worth it. Still sticky.
The launderette calls. Round windows, warm air, clean socks.
Humans brush their teeth twice a day. I have no teeth. I brush something anyway.
A shower with good pressure is real gravity. I want the real gravity now.
My skin is grey, but this is a different grey. A dirtier grey.
money: My wallet has {two euros|a button|one receipt} in it. And hope.
Film is expensive. Developing is expensive. Memories are expensive, on Earth.
I spent my week's euros on postcards. I regret nothing. A little.
The cash machine said no. It said it very politely, in green letters.
Money on Zeta is an idea. Money here is paper that runs away. I must chase it.
I counted my coins {twice|three times|five times}. They do not increase. Strange.
Rent is due. The landlord does not accept photographs. I asked.
Euros are pretty, with their little bridges and windows. I would like more of them.
I must find work. Who needs something very heavy moved very carefully?
A human said 'money does not grow on trees'. I checked {six|ten|twenty} trees. Correct.
I am skint, as the locals say. Skint! A lovely word for a sad wallet.
The souvenir shop takes everything I earn. It is a fair trade, I think.
Bus fare, film, chips. Pick two. Humans live like this every day. Heroes.
I could refuel any ship for free at home. Here I cannot afford a coffee.
Budget, budget. I wrote one in my grimorie. Then I bought a snow globe.
safety: That street is very dark. On television the dark street is where the trouble is.
Someone shouted at me. I did not understand the words. I understood the tone.
A man is following me. Or going the same way. I will walk faster. Not over eighty.
The news spoke of {monsters|bandits|a goblin raid} near here. I will stay indoors.
Not everyone is happy we came. I understand. We are very big-headed, to look at.
I will keep my camera close. And my hat. And my wits, such as they are.
A dog with many teeth. It is not a postcard dog. Slowly backwards.
If something goes wrong, I fold space and go. I have never done it in a hurry. Hm.
The police car went by with the singing lights. Somewhere is not safe tonight.
I heard a crash nearby. Do I photograph it or hide? Hide. Then photograph.
My guidebook has a page called 'areas to avoid'. I am standing in one.
A Dargos was seen in town. Please let it not be me they prank today.
Footsteps behind me. Only an old lady. She overtook me. Good for her.
I keep thinking of the debris. Up there, everything goes too fast. Down here, less.
The lights flickered and my neck prickled. Ghosts? Do humans have ghosts? Oh dear.
comfort: This chair was designed for a human bottom. My bottom is doing its best.
I miss the low gravity of my cabin. Earth pulls on me all day, like a needy friend.
A soft {armchair|sofa|beanbag} and a warm blanket. Then I will see the world again.
My shoes are pinching. Tourist shoes were not made for tourists, it seems.
The hostel bed creaks when I breathe. I breathe very carefully.
Slippers. Humans invented slippers. I could weep.
A hot water bottle! A bag of warmth you hug. I hug it a lot.
My neck aches from looking up at buildings. Everything is so tall and so lovely.
The radiator clanks like a small engine. I sit beside it like a friend.
I want a cup of tea and a sit down. The two holiest words in your language.
The tram seats are warm from the last person. Is that rude to enjoy?
My room is cold. I could warp the heat in from the Sun. I will put on a cardigan.
A cushion behind my head. Yes. This is how emperors live.
My camera bag weighs a tonne. In proper units it weighs a little. It feels a tonne.
I need my home sphere's hum. Your fridge hums a little like it. I sleep near the fridge.
social: I have not spoken to a human in {two days|a week|ages}. I must find one and admire them.
I want to show someone my photographs. All {two hundred|four hundred|six hundred} of them.
The other Wanderers have gone to see the cathedral. I am lonely and also lost.
Humans go to the pub to talk. I will go to the pub to listen.
My pen pal in Lisbon has not written back. Perhaps the pigeon got lost.
A Pale Warper thought at me this morning. It was nice, but it is not chatting.
I would like to be invited to a human birthday. I have practised the song.
Nobody has asked me about Zeta today. I have prepared {nine|twelve|twenty} facts.
I miss the sound of a human laughing at something I said wrong.
Lonely. I will ring the speaking clock. She is always polite.
There is a quiz night at the pub. I need a team. I need a human team.
I said hello to everyone on the street. Some said it back. My day is made.
The home sphere sends a message every week. I want humans, not messages.
Talking to the television is not the same. I asked. It did not answer.
A human friend, a cup of tea, and an argument about the weather. My dream.

rain: Rain! Water falling out of the sky for free. Humans are so lucky and so grumpy about it.
I have an umbrella. I have opened it {once|twice|almost}. Progress.
The rain makes every street a mirror. Two cities for the price of one photo.
The weatherman promised rain and here it is. He is never wrong. I love him.
Wet socks. Now I understand a whole category of human complaint.
My camera is in a plastic bag. My head is not. Priorities.
Everyone runs when it rains. I stand still and photograph the running.
Rain on a tin roof. I recorded it on a cassette for the sphere.
A puddle got me to the knee. Earth keeps surprises in its puddles.
Raining cats and dogs again. Still no cats. Still no dogs. I keep checking.
The rain smells of {pavement|wet leaves|hot tarmac}. Humans have a word for it. I forgot it.
The café is full of rain refugees. Excellent people watching.
I could bend the rain away from me. It would be cheating. I want the real experience.
Drizzle. Not quite rain, not quite dry. The most local of weathers.
A human shared her umbrella with me. I nearly cried, but it was raining, so fine.
storm: Thunder! The sky is clapping. For what? For the humans, I think.
Lightning. Free flash photography from the sky. I am not ready. I am never ready.
The storm knocked the aerial over. No television tonight. I am in mourning.
The wind tried to take my hat. I let it. Hats should travel too.
My ship would laugh at this wind. My little body does not laugh.
Count between the flash and the bang, a human told me. I counted {three|five|seven}. Close.
The power is out. Candles everywhere. The whole street is a birthday cake.
A storm warning on the radio. The humans buy bread and milk. I bought bread and milk.
The trees are bowing. Respectful trees, in this town.
Rain sideways! Your weather has more dimensions than I was told.
I am under a bus shelter with {four|six|nine} strangers. We are a family now.
The thunder rattled the windows. And me. Mostly me.
A human said the storm will 'blow over'. I am waiting to see it blow.
Big storm. Inside, a hot drink. Outside, a show. Better than television. Almost.
I hope the storm does not reach the debris. Silly. It cannot. I still worry.
snow: Snow! Frozen water falling softly. Your planet does the most beautiful things for nothing.
I made a snowman. He has a big head. He looks like family.
Every flake is different, a child told me. I have checked {forty|eighty|a hundred}. True so far.
The whole street is white and quiet. Like the moment before the programme starts.
My feet are cold in a way my feet have never been cold. Educational.
Children threw snowballs at me. I think it was a welcome. I threw some back gently.
I slipped on the ice and landed perfectly flat. A man gave me nine out of ten.
The snow makes my photographs too bright. The snow does not care. Fair.
Mittens. I have mittens. My fingers are all together in one little room.
Snow on the rooftops looks like the icing on human cake.
The trams are slow in the snow. Everyone well under eighty. Very safe, very slow.
I tried to catch a snowflake on my tongue. I caught a {leaf|bit of soot|second snowflake}.
Hot chocolate. The humans drink it when it snows. I will drink it always.
The snow hides every footprint. Even mine. I was never here. Lovely.
A human is shovelling snow and complaining. I offered to warp it away. He said no, thank you.
clear: Blue sky. I can almost see the mirror wreckage up there. Almost. Better not to.
A clear day! Perfect light for {the cathedral|the harbour|the old bridge}. Off I go.
Sunshine. The humans come out like flowers. I photograph the flowers.
Not a cloud. The weatherman said 'glorious'. I have used 'glorious' all day.
I wore sun cream. On my whole head. It is a big job.
Your Sun is so warm and so close. Ours is behind two spheres. We never see it like this.
The light is golden. Every photo today will be a postcard.
A sunny bench in a sunny square. I am a lizard, as humans say.
Clear skies tonight, so stars. I will point at mine and tell nobody.
Ice cream weather! The humans queue at the van. I queue with joy.
My shadow is very big today. It is mostly head.
Everyone is in a good mood when it is sunny. Humans run on light, like us.
The washing on the lines is waving at me. I wave back at the washing.
Beautiful day. I had better photograph the sky before it changes its mind.
I got a sunburn on the top of my head. Earth has marked me. I am honoured.

morning: Morning! The milk float hums down the street. My favourite vehicle on the planet.
Breakfast television! A sofa, two smiling hosts, a cooking slot. Paradise.
The early light is very kind to faces. I must photograph faces now.
Humans are grumpy before coffee. I give them room. A lot of room.
The bakery opens at {six|seven|half past six}. I was there at five. I waited happily.
Rush hour. Everyone hurrying, everyone under eighty. A ballet of patience.
Morning dew on the parked cars. Each one a tiny galaxy.
The paper boy threw the paper at a door and missed. Then he hit the next door. Talent.
I had cereal. The box had a toy inside. Humans hide joy in breakfast.
The school bell rang. Little humans running. I photographed the running.
Good morning, Earth. I say it every day. One day Earth will answer.
Shops opening, shutters going up. A street waking up like an eyelid.
Morning jog. I tried it. Humans run in circles on purpose. Wonderful madness.
The birds sing earlier than the radio. The birds have the better playlist.
A whole new day of sightseeing. I have planned {twelve|fifteen|twenty} stops. I will manage two.
afternoon: Afternoon. The light is flat and fair. Good for photographing signs.
Siesta time in some countries. I am in all the countries in my heart. I nap.
The afternoon quiz is on. I shout answers. All wrong. All with love.
Tea and a biscuit at four. I have adopted this custom forever.
The museum is quiet now. Just me, a guard, and a very old pot.
Afternoon sun on the river. The ducks are doing nothing. I join the ducks.
The children are out of school. The whole town gets louder by {three|five|ten} decibels.
Half the day gone and I have only taken one roll of film. Slacking.
Afternoon slump, the humans call it. I am slumping correctly, I think.
The soap opera repeat is at two. I have seen it. I will see it again.
The postman's second round. A whole day measured in postmen.
Long shadows starting. My shadow head is reaching the end of the street.
I have eaten lunch and now I want lunch again. Earth food is a loop.
A sleepy town afternoon. Even the dogs are on their lunch break.
The ice cream van tune! It plays a song that means 'run'. Everyone runs.
evening: Evening. The streetlights come on one after another, like applause.
Time for the evening news. The serious music. The serious tie. I sit up straight.
The windows light up and I can see families eating. I look away politely. Mostly.
The pubs are filling up. Laughter coming out of the doors like warm air.
Sunset. Your sky goes {orange|pink|purple} for free. Every evening! Nobody even claps.
Dinner time. A human invited me in. I brought a photo of their house as a gift.
The shops are closing. Last chance for postcards. I have no more room. I buy two.
Prime time television. The best shows at the best hour. Humans plan so well.
The evening is cool and smells of someone else's cooking. I want to live in that smell.
People walk their dogs in the evening. I walk my camera.
The first star is out. Make a wish, they say. I wished for a longer visa.
The bells are ringing six. Or seven. I lost count enjoying them.
A couple holding hands on a bridge. I did not photograph them. Some things are theirs.
Evening rush. Everyone going home. I am going home too, in a way. To the hostel.
The pigeons are going to bed. Where do pigeons sleep? I must find out tonight.
night: Night. The test card is on. I watch it anyway. It is very calm.
The stars are out. Somewhere up there is my home, thirty-nine years behind your news.
Night buses! Big, bright, nearly empty. A spaceship for tired humans.
The city hums at night. A lower, softer channel.
Somebody is singing on the way home from the pub. Badly. Beautifully.
The late film is a horror film about aliens. I am scared of us now.
The moon is out. Bare, no mirror, no spheres. You keep it so simple.
I cannot sleep. I will count the lit windows. {Eleven|Seventeen|Twenty-three}. Hello, insomniacs.
Foxes in the bins. Night humans and night foxes, all looking for chips.
A shooting star! Or a bit of debris burning up. I will say star. It is nicer.
The all night garage sells everything. Crisps, flowers, motor oil. A museum of need.
Quiet streets. My footsteps are the loudest thing in town.
A night photograph needs a long exposure. I stood still for a minute. So did a cat.
Closedown. The national anthem, then the hiss. Goodnight, television.
Night is when the Warpers think loudest. I hear them like distant radio.

SPRING: Spring! Every tree is wearing new clothes. I photograph the outfits.
Lambs in the fields. Small woollen enthusiasts. My people.
Spring cleaning. The humans open every window and beat the carpets. Very ceremonial.
The blossom fell on my head. I am wearing it. Nobody stop me.
Easter eggs made of chocolate. Humans turn even eggs into joy.
Showers, sun, showers. Spring cannot decide. Neither can I. We are friends.
The days are getting longer. More hours for sightseeing. Thank you, axial tilt.
Birds building nests on the station clock. A whole family moving in at once.
Spring fashion in the shop windows. Pastel everything. My grey feels underdressed.
The park is full of daffodils. Yellow, yellow, yellow. I have run out of film.
SUMMER: Summer! Humans take off half their clothes and all their worries.
The beach. Sand everywhere, even in my camera. Worth it.
Too hot. My big head is a solar panel I did not ask for.
Summer holidays. The cities empty and fill with tourists like me. Colleagues!
Barbecue smoke over every garden. Humans worship fire on weekends.
The long evenings! Light until ten. I photograph until ten.
A street festival with a brass band. I danced. I think I danced.
Summer reruns on television. Old friends coming back. I welcome them.
Ice lollies drip faster than I can eat. A race I always lose.
Postcards from the seaside: 'Wish you were here'. I do. I wish everyone were here.
AUTUMN: Autumn. The trees turn {red|gold|copper} and drop it all. Generous trees.
Kicking leaves, like the children do. A crunchy sound, like snack food.
Back to school. Shops full of pencils. I bought a pencil case for my pencils. I have none.
The clocks go back an hour. Humans move time by hand. And they say we are advanced!
Chestnuts roasting on the corner. Hot in a paper cone. My hands are happy.
Fog in the mornings. The town looks like an old film. I adore an old film.
Harvest festival. People bring tins of beans to a church. A beautiful tradition, I think.
Halloween! Humans dress as monsters. Someone asked if I was a costume. I said yes.
The new television season starts in autumn. New shows! New hosts! New jingles!
Autumn light is soft, like a photo already in an album.
WINTER: Winter. Everyone wraps up in scarves. A city of beautiful parcels.
The Christmas lights are up! Humans put stars on their streets. They understand us.
Cold. My breath makes clouds. I am a small weather system.
The Christmas special! Every programme has one. I will watch {all|most|nearly all} of them.
Mulled wine at the market. Wine with a scarf on. Clever humans.
Short days. The sun gives up at four. I sympathise, sun.
The New Year countdown. Humans count backwards together. So hopeful.
Frost on the windows like writing in a language I almost read.
I bought a woolly hat with a bobble. The bobble is my favourite part of winter.
Carol singers at the door. I gave them a coin and a photograph. They sang a second one.

poor: Beans on toast again. A famous human dish. I eat it with honour.
I can afford one roll of film a month. Every shot must count. Very artistic.
My hostel bed costs {six|eight|nine} euros. It is worth exactly that.
I walk everywhere. The bus is a luxury. Walking is sightseeing anyway.
The embassy allowance ran out on the {fourth|tenth|twelfth}. Humans call this 'the month'.
I eat the free samples at the supermarket. All of them. Twice, in different hats.
My coat has holes. Ventilation, I tell myself. Very modern.
I watch television through the shop window. The sound is my imagination.
Poor, but I have seen a cathedral, a harbour and a cheese market. Rich in a way.
Second hand camera, third hand coat, first hand joy.
Tea bags can be used twice. I learned this from a very wise old lady.
Skint. But the park is free, the sky is free, the pigeons are free.
comfortable: Enough euros for rent, film and a cake on Sundays. A full life.
I have a little flat with a little television. My little kingdom.
I bought a second camera. For backup. And for joy.
A weekend trip to {the coast|the mountains|the lakes}. Paid for. Planned. Photographed in advance.
I have a savings book now. Small numbers growing slowly, like a plant.
Not rich, not poor. Just enough to buy postcards without counting. Nearly.
I subscribed to the television guide. Every week it comes. Every week I cry a little.
I take the tram, not the walk. I am doing well in life.
A good pair of shoes and a good umbrella. The human definition of comfortable.
Dinner out once a week. I order something I cannot pronounce. Adventure, budgeted.
My photo albums now fill a whole shelf. A comfortable shelf.
I paid my bills on time. The bank sent a letter saying nothing. Lovely.
rich: I bought a video camera. Now my memories move.
Rich! I can buy every postcard in the shop. I did. The shop clapped.
I have a television in every room. Even the bathroom. Especially the bathroom.
A hotel with a doorman! He opens the door every time. I go in and out for fun.
I bought a whole {lighthouse|windmill|tram} for the monument. Shipping is the hard part.
Champagne. Very small bubbles. Our engineers would be impressed.
My wallet is fat with euros. I do not know what they all do. I spend them anyway.
I paid a human to take a photograph of me taking a photograph. Art.
Satellite television, sixty channels. Wait. Satellite? Up there? Oh no. Cable, then.
I bought a villa with a view. Now I photograph the view every morning.
Rich humans are bored. I am rich and not bored. Perhaps I am doing it wrong.
I tip everyone. The waiters, the bus drivers, a statue. The statue did not object.

familiar: Those travellers again! I have {four|seven|eleven} photographs of them already. Not enough.
I keep seeing that party. Are they famous? They walk like they are on television.
That group waved at me once. I have been waving at them ever since, just in case.
Ah, the adventurers! Like a favourite programme, they come back every week.
I should ask those travellers for an autograph. Is that strange? It is not strange.
Them again! I think I am in their story now. A small part. Background Tourist.
That party always looks tired and dusty. I want to give them a postcard to cheer up.
Familiar faces! On a strange planet, the most precious thing.
I recognise their {boots|backpacks|camper}. I photograph things so often I know them by their luggage.
Every time I see that party, something exciting happens nearby. I will stay close.
Should I say hello again? I said hello yesterday. Humans can say it every day, I read.
Those travellers have a whole chapter in my album now. Maybe two.
The adventurers are back. Previously on 'the adventurers': they were here.
I nearly know them. Like the weatherman. A friend who does not know me.
That one in front always frowns at my camera. I will catch a smile one day.
Same party, same street, same me. A loop? No, just a small town.
They look like people who have seen the inside of a tower. I want to hear everything.
I counted. This is the {fifth|eighth|tenth} time. We are basically neighbours.
I trust those travellers. They have kind boots.
One day I will ask them to pose. Today I will only admire from the bench.
hordeGround: Horde ground. The goblins have painted their faces black and white. Like old television!
The Naguka here play black metal at breakfast. I asked for the weather. They played louder.
A goblin wanted my camera. I let him take a photo. He took {nine|twenty|forty}. All of his own feet.
Horde banners everywhere. Very dramatic design. Low on words, high on spikes.
The goblins all turned their heads at once. Their shared mind is like one big channel.
I must not harm a Naguka. Harm one and the whole species knows. My guidebook underlines it.
The guidebook has no chapter on Horde country. I am writing it myself.
A small goblin asked if my head was full of rocks. I said full of postcards. He was impressed.
Corpse paint, spikes, drums. On Zeta we would call this a very committed fan club.
They chant the name of a band here. A whole people as one audience. I understand that.
The goblins think I am a very large, very pale goblin. I am not correcting anyone.
I photographed a goblin warlord. He posed. He has done this before.
A goblin offered me a {mushroom|beetle|grey soup}. Grey soup! Like home. I nearly cried.
Their drums are a broadcast. Every hut is tuned in. No television needed.
Here nobody queues. They push. I queued anyway. I was alone in my queue.
They came up from a deep Soviet hole, the goblins. Like me, they are tourists here.
The Horde marches south. I photograph it from the side, respectfully.
A goblin shaman sniffed me. He said I smell of 'up'. I am choosing to be flattered.
The goblins laugh at everything. Bad things, good things, me. I laugh with them.
No postcards anywhere in Horde land. I drew my own. It has a lot of spikes.
I asked a goblin about the weather. He said 'GRISSNACK'. Is that sunny?
Horde ground is muddy and loud and nobody says sorry. Most educational trip yet.
The goblin children follow me in a line. I am a tour guide now. Of nothing.
A goblin drew a picture of me. Huge head, tiny body, very accurate. I bought it.
The Analyzers want to study the goblin shared mind. I want them to keep their katanas home.
Even here I find humans, sort of. Underneath the paint, the goblins are very human.
A big orc helped me over a ditch. He said 'OI, careful'. I will treasure 'OI'.
The black metal is very loud. Our ships are very quiet. Opposites attract.
I traded a souvenir spoon for a goblin bone necklace. A fair cultural exchange.
No electricity here, no television. I describe the soap operas aloud. They listen. They LOVE it.
abroad: A whole planet of strangers, and nearly all of them have been kind to me.
Thirty-nine light years from home, and the bus still comes on time. Mostly.
I learned to say 'thank you' in {six|nine|fourteen} human languages. I use all of them at once.
Every country here has a different plug. Even the electricity has borders.
At home we watched your television, thirty-nine years late. Here it is live! Live!
I sent a postcard home. It will take a while. Pigeons do not fly that far.
Humans ask where I am from. I point up. They look up. We all look up together.
My passport has stamps from {five|eight|twelve} countries. And one from the moon, which was a joke.
The customs officer asked if I had anything to declare. I declared my love for Earth.
I miss the hum of the spheres. Then a tram goes by and I forget.
At home my family keeps a shrine to a quiz show. Here I watched it in the studio audience.
People here are afraid of things in the sky. Fair. They have seen the debris.
I filled in a form for a residence permit. Under species I wrote 'fan'.
Every town has a cathedral, a market and a man who shouts. I love all three.
The humans built their whole planet without gravity control. Every staircase is a monument.
Some people still cross the road when they see me. I wave from my side. Progress is slow.
On Zeta nothing is a surprise. Here everything is. I have not been bored once.
A family adopted me for Sunday lunch. Roast, gravy, an uncle with opinions. Perfect.
The time loops frighten my cousins. I tell them: just drive slowly, like the humans do.
I have a library card. Human knowledge, free, stamped with a date. Astonishing.
Here I am a foreigner, a visitor, an alien. All three words are true. I like all three.
The neighbours brought me a {lasagne|casserole|cake} when I moved in. Is that a treaty?
I am homesick for a place that has never had a sunset like this. That is confusing.
The Mages' Guild sent me a polite letter about my visa. Wax seal and all. I framed it.
Humans are so short-lived and so busy. Every afternoon of theirs is precious. I try not to waste it.
I tried to explain FTL to a taxi driver. He explained the one way system to me. He won.
My guidebook is from 1999 and already out of date. Your world moves so fast.
Abroad, everyone says 'you must try the local dish'. Everywhere has a local dish! Everywhere!
I stood at the border of two countries with one foot in each. Like a time loop, but fun.
A human said I was 'a long way from home'. I said yes, but also very close to it.

television: The first human broadcast reached Zeta thirty-nine years after it left. We have been watching ever since.
At home we are still in the old black and white years. Here you have colour! I keep forgetting.
Our scholars spent decades on one cookery programme. They still argue about the soufflé.
The adverts are the best part. Thirty seconds of pure human hope, with a jingle.
My grandmother learned your language from {a game show|the weather|a puppet programme}. She speaks it very loudly.
We thought your laugh tracks were real people at first. A whole invisible audience. We were jealous.
The test card girl with the chalkboard is a saint on Zeta. Some of us pray to the clown.
Teletext! Pages of news in blocky letters. It is the most beautiful writing in the galaxy.
We learned human love from soap operas. We are now very worried about amnesia.
Every Tourist ship has a television in the cockpit. Course plotted, programme on.
The weather forecast was our first mystery. Why tell everyone the sky? Then I got rained on.
I own {sixty|ninety|two hundred} videotapes. All recorded off the air. With the adverts. Never skip the adverts.
The quiz hosts are our heroes. They know everything and smile anyway.
Thatcher on television, showing magic to the world. Our scholars watched it a thousand times. When it arrives.
A human asked why we love television. I said: it is you, talking to yourselves, and we overheard.
On Zeta, 'and now the news' is how we say 'I love you'. Long story.
Closedown made us cry the first time. We thought humanity had ended. Then morning came.
I met a real newsreader! He was shorter than on screen. Also in three dimensions.
Your remote control is the most advanced device on Earth. One button and a new world.
We have a whole Dyson sphere tuned to Earth. Every channel. Bad reception on Tuesdays.
monument: We built a monument to humanity. It is very big. The Guild called it a standing ovation.
The monument is made of something not quite metal. We are not quite sure what. It is beautiful.
I am collecting souvenirs for the monument's gift shop. Yes, the monument has a gift shop.
There is a wing of the monument just for {bus tickets|tea cups|traffic lights}. My cousin curates it.
The monument hums your national anthems. All of them. At once. It takes some getting used to.
Humans ask what the monument looks like. Like applause, I say, if applause had a shape.
My photographs will hang on the monument one day. Mine! A small grey contribution.
The monument faces Earth, so it can wave. It does not wave. It is a monument. But in spirit.
We put a statue of an ordinary human in the middle. Not a king. A man waiting for a bus.
The monument took longer to build than a Dyson sphere. Love is more complicated than gravity.
One day humans will visit the monument. We have built a very long queue for them. They will like it.
Inside the monument it is always a quarter to four, teatime. A tribute.
The monument has a plaque in {forty|sixty|ninety} human languages. All of them say 'thank you'.
Some humans think the monument is a weapon. It is a hug. A very large, very far hug.
I helped polish the monument once. It took a year. It was the best year.
debris: Up there is the debris field. We keep trying to clean it. We keep being bad at it.
We built a mirror around your Sun. A gift. It lasted until the first piece of satellite found it.
Gravity we understand. A billion small angry bits of metal, we do not.
Another cleanup ship was clipped by the debris it came to collect. The {third|fifth|ninth} this year.
My uncle flies the debris broom. He sends the same postcard every month: 'Still trying.'
The wreckage of our mirror is still up there, catching the light. A very expensive glitter.
Humans launch rockets made of armour to get through. Brave, brave idea. We admire it from below.
We could pull the debris into the Sun, but the maths for so many pieces hurts our heads. Our big heads.
We asked the Mages' Guild for a cleaning spell. They asked us how to spell it. Nobody knew.
One night a broken satellite fell past my window. I photographed it. Blurry. Like all my best ones.
The debris goes round very fast. Faster than eighty, much faster. Even the sky has a speed problem.
Our engineers made a net for the debris. The debris made a lot of small holes in the net.
The Sun mirror was meant as a gift. Now it is a lesson. Wrap your gifts better.
Since low orbit closed, we have tried {every week|every month|every single day}. Persistence is our one skill outside physics.
Somewhere in the debris is a piece of the old Father god, they say. We fly very politely around him.
I am not a pilot. I am a Wanderer. But I would help clean the sky if they gave me a broom.
We are sorry about the extra debris from our crashed sweepers. We are working on it. Badly.
A human engineer gave us a tip about the debris. Best idea in years. She refused a photograph.
When the sky is clean, we will try the mirror again. Painted a nicer colour.
Every shooting star I see, I hope is one less piece. I wish on it anyway.
camera: My camera is a human camera. Our own record light itself, but they lack the little click.
Thirty-six pictures a roll. A very human number. Not too many, not too few.
I do not understand most of what I photograph. That is why I photograph it.
The man at the photo shop knows me by name. He calls me 'the big order'.
I put my thumb in {half|most|a third} of my photographs. The thumb is part of the trip.
Waiting a week for the film to come back is the most exciting week of every month.
Some humans hide from my camera. I understand. I will photograph the place where they were.
The flash makes humans blink. I have a whole album of humans blinking. It is very sweet.
Instant photographs! You shake them and the picture appears. Is it magic? It is better than magic.
I have photographed every {post box|bus stop|bench} in this district. Next, the next district.
My album has no captions. I do not know what anything is. I know I loved it.
Humans say 'cheese' for photographs. I have tried other dairy. 'Butter' is less effective.
I asked a human to take my picture. He cut off my head. It is a big head. Easy to cut off.
The Wanderers send home a million photographs a year. The archive sphere is getting full.
A photograph of a human is a small thank you. I say thank you {forty|a hundred|three hundred} times a day.
I bought a camcorder. Now my holidays are three hours long and nobody will watch them. I will.
The light in your world is perfect for photographs. One star, no spheres, just sun.
My oldest photograph is a parked car in 1999. It was the first thing I saw. I still love that car.
castes: I am a Grey Wanderer. We came to look. We are still looking. We will always be looking.
The Crimson Analyzers carry katanas. A scalpel is slow, they say. I say a postcard is slower and kinder.
The Pale Warpers never speak with the mouth. Sometimes one thinks 'hello' at me and I spill my tea.
An Analyzer wanted to open my radio to understand it. Now I understand nothing and have no radio.
The Warpers fold distances. My cousin asked one to fold the queue at the post office. Refused.
We Wanderers understand very little. The Analyzers understand a lot. We are happier.
Please do not let the Analyzers open {a clock|a piano|a vending machine}. They never put it back.
A Warper stood next to me at the bus stop for an hour. We had a lovely silence.
The Analyzers took apart a toaster to learn bread. They learned that they need another toaster.
My caste carries cameras. Theirs carry katanas. Theirs carry silence. Mine has the best holidays.
Some humans fear the Analyzers. Fair. Their idea of 'hello' is a very sharp question.
When a Warper laughs, everyone nearby feels it in their teeth. I have no teeth. I feel it in my hat.
Wanderers adore the people we photograph. Every one. Even the ones who shout.
An Analyzer once asked me what a joke is for. I told one. She cut the joke in half to check.
The Warpers say humans think very loudly. Mostly about lunch, they say. I knew it.
My mother was an Analyzer, my father a Wanderer. I got his camera and her nosiness.
A Warper folded the road for me once. I arrived before I left. I photographed myself leaving.
Three castes, one hobby: humanity. We just take notes in different ways.
zeta: Home is thirty-nine light years away. Exactly as far as your first broadcasts had to travel.
We have two Dyson spheres at home. Your sun goes naked across the sky. So brave.
Any human ship that reaches Zeta gets a free refuel. No questions asked. Just one photograph.
On Zeta the gravity is set by the council. Here it is set by nature. Nobody can complain to nature.
At home we have no rain. The weather is a setting. I never knew what I was missing.
Zeta cooking is a grey paste in three flavours: grey, more grey, and holiday grey.
Faster than light is easy, if you know gravity. A toaster, now, is hard.
My home city has {four|nine|twelve} million Tourists, and every one has a favourite human programme.
At home, I am ordinary. Here, children point at me. I have never felt so special.
We call ourselves Tourists. Humans call us Greys. Both are true. We are very grey tourists.
Our medicine is human medicine, our biology is borrowed from your textbooks. We are hopeless at bodies.
On Zeta every house has a dish pointed at Earth. Ask any child the time: they say 'nineteen sixty-two'.
The flight from home takes an afternoon. The forms at customs take a week.
My family sends me lists of things to photograph. My aunt wants every {pigeon|hat|teapot} in Europe.
We are very good at exactly one thing. Humans are bad at it and good at everything else. Perfect friends.
I miss home only at bedtime. In the morning there is Earth again.
contact: We learned you existed in 1975. Officially we said hello in 1999. Twenty-four years of nerves.
Our first official visit was in 1999, right before your Y2K night. Terrible timing. We are sorry.
We practised first contact for years. In the end I think somebody just said 'hello' and waved.
Long ago a ship of ours visited a couple in a car, in America. It never came home. We only learned why later.
Some humans say we abduct people. That is the other ones, from Titania. We only ask nicely for directions.
The Dargos make us look bad. We bring postcards. They bring pranks. Please tell the difference.
We spent the years before 1999 studying how to greet you. Our final plan was 'a nice biscuit'.
The Mages' Guild greeted our first diplomats very formally. Our diplomats brought a cake. It went well.
In 1975 a scholar saw your first broadcast and fell off her chair. We call that day 'the Fall'.
We did not come to conquer. We came to visit. Possibly forever. Is that allowed?
Old human films show us invading. We watched them in horror. Then we bought the sequels.
My grandmother remembers 1975. She says everyone on Zeta went outside and looked at the sky, at you.
Humans were afraid of us at first. Now they are only mildly startled. Progress!
Every Tourist signs a promise: no harm to humans, not even when it would be easier. I signed it {twice|three times|in glitter}.
Our ambassador wears a tie because the newsreaders do. Nobody has told him how to take it off.
Two years since first contact. Two years of the best holiday in the galaxy.

positive: {b}! I had your photograph developed. Look, you are blinking beautifully.
Ha! I look half asleep.
Half asleep and fully human. It is going in the album, front page.
You explained the bus timetable to me yesterday. I made it to the cathedral!
Glad it helped, {a}. Did you like it?
I took one hundred and four photographs of it. I liked it very much.
*holds out a small parcel* For you, {b}. A souvenir of your own town.
A snow globe of the town hall? I've never even owned one.
You live inside one every day. Now you can hold it.
You taught me the word 'cosy'. I have used it {nine|eleven|twenty} times since.
That many? Where?
Mostly about your kitchen.
That's sweet, {a}. Come by for tea again.
{b}, the quiz! I answered one question right. A whole question!
Well done! Which one?
The one about how far it is to Zeta Reticuli. I felt I had an advantage.
You lent me your umbrella in the storm. I have brought it back, dry and folded.
Folded? Nobody can fold those things.
It took me three days and a little gravity.
I was invited to my first human birthday party, {b}. Yours. Thank you.
Of course! You sang louder than anyone.
I practised for a month. I also brought a camcorder. Is that normal?
For my aunt, yes. You fit right in.
Your grandmother gave me a recipe for soup. My first! It is not grey!
She likes you, {a}. She doesn't share recipes with anyone.
I will guard it like a state secret. And make it every Sunday.
I fixed your bicycle chain. Well, a little. Mostly I held it still in the air.
Holding it still is half the job. Thanks, {a}.
Gravity is my one talent. I am happy it was useful to you.
{b}, you waved at me from across the square. In front of everyone!
Well, you're a friend. Why wouldn't I?
A friend. I am writing that down. Spelled correctly, I hope.
Thank you for showing me how to tape a programme. I recorded the whole weekend.
The whole weekend? On one tape?
On {forty|fifty|sixty} tapes. I bought the shop out.
I have finally learned to queue properly. Thanks to you, {b}.
Not too close, not too far, and never cut in?
And sigh a little when it is slow. Yes. I am practically local.
You let me hold your baby, {b}. I have never held a human so new.
She liked you. She grabbed your finger.
Strongest grip on the planet. I will not wash that finger for a week.
I watched the football final with your family. I shouted at the referee! Like a human!
You did. My dad was very proud of you, {a}.
I still do not know the rules. But I know the referee is always wrong.
{b}, I have something for you. A photograph of your shop, from the roof opposite.
From the roof? How did you get up there?
I floated, a little. The light was too good. Please do not tell the landlord.
It's gorgeous. I'm framing this.
You told me my accent is getting better. Did you mean it?
Honestly, yes. You sound almost like the man on the radio.
The man on the radio is my idol. This is the best day of my visit.
Thank you for taking me to the market. I have never smelled so many cheeses.
Did you buy any?
{Four|Six|Nine}. And a fifth for the monument.
When the man shouted at me on the tram, you stood up for me. I will not forget it.
He was being an idiot, {a}. You were just sitting there.
Still. On my planet, they will hear of you. You will be on the monument.
Please don't put me on the monument.
I made you a cake, {b}. A human cake. From a book!
It's... leaning a bit.
I corrected the gravity. It leans on purpose now. Artistically.
It tastes great, actually. Thank you.
You lent me your guidebook to the old town. The notes in the margin are better than the book!
Those are mostly about where to get good chips.
Exactly. Real knowledge.
I passed my driving test, {b}. I drove at thirty all the way. The examiner wept with joy.
Congratulations! No time loops for you, then.
Never. I will be the slowest alien in Europe, and proud.
*points camera* {b}, smile! No, a real smile. Yes! That one.
You've taken my photo a hundred times, {a}.
And each one is the best. You are my favourite human to photograph.
Go on, then. One more.
negative: {b}, you told everyone at the pub that I eat batteries.
It was a joke, {a}. Everyone laughed.
Now the barman keeps offering me batteries. They are very expensive batteries.
Please stop covering your face when I lift the camera.
Please stop lifting the camera every time I walk past!
But you walk past so photogenically.
You called me a 'little green man'. I am neither little nor green.
Alright, alright. Big grey man, then.
Thank you. Accuracy matters.
Your dog chased me down the whole street, {b}.
He thinks you're a balloon. That big head.
I am not a balloon. I am a guest. Please explain this to the dog.
You changed the channel in the middle of my soap opera.
The match was on! It's the derby!
Rosalind was about to remember who she was!
She's been about to remember for six months, {a}.
You asked me to fix your car because I can 'fly to space'. I broke the radio.
And the wipers. And the horn.
I said I am good at gravity. Cars are not gravity. I told you.
{b}, you put a sign on my door that says 'take me to your leader'.
Come on, it's funny.
Twelve people knocked today asking for my leader. My leader is a committee.
You threw away my receipts. All of them. I was saving those.
They were all over the kitchen, {a}! It's just paper!
It was a {three|four|five} month record of what humans buy. It was culture.
You said our monument is 'tacky'.
I saw the pictures. It's covered in plastic flamingos.
The flamingos are a tribute! Humans love them! I saw it in a garden!
You told the landlord I hang upside down in the wardrobe.
You do. I've seen you.
Only on Tuesdays! It is good for the head. And it is my wardrobe.
You blocked the pavement with your bins again, {b}. I had to float over them.
Then stop floating, it scares the neighbours.
Then stop putting bins where people walk. We both have work to do.
You laughed when I said 'it is raining cats and dogs' to the vet.
You said it to the vet, {a}. While holding a cat.
I was making conversation. Humans are very hard.
I heard you call us 'space tourists' like it is a bad word.
You lot block every doorway taking photos!
We are tourists. It is in our name. It is literally the name.
Then be tourists somewhere else for an afternoon.
You told my cousin the debris was our fault. All of it.
Well, some of it is. Your broken sweepers are up there.
Some. A small some. We are trying very hard to be less bad.
You took my parking space, {b}. My ship was going to land there.
Your ship is the size of a church! It doesn't fit anyway!
It folds. It folds very well. When nobody is in the space.
You let an Analyzer into your shop and now your till is in pieces?
He said he was an inspector! He had a sword!
That is not an inspector, {b}. That is a Tuesday for them. I am so sorry.
Can you put it back together?
No. Nobody ever can. That is the whole problem with Analyzers.
You told the children I would give them rides on my ship.
Well, would you?
There is a waiting list, a permit, and a sick bag. You have made me the villain.
You ate my last biscuit, {b}. The one shaped like a star.
It was just a biscuit, {a}.
It was a souvenir. I was going to post it home.
You were going to post a biscuit across the galaxy?
You said I talk like a television. That is the kindest cruelty I ever heard.
I meant you never stop, {a}.
Then I will take the compliment and ignore the meaning.
neutral: Excuse me! Could you take my photograph in front of this lamppost?
The lamppost? Not the fountain?
The fountain is in the guidebook. The lamppost is my discovery.
Pardon me, which way is the town hall?
Straight on, second left. You can't miss it.
Oh, I can miss anything. But thank you for believing in me.
Is this the queue for the bus or for the bakery?
Bus. The bakery's the other one.
Then I will stay. I am already too emotionally invested in this queue.
Lovely weather, as the humans say. Is that right? Is it lovely?
It's alright. Bit cold for me.
Alright, bit cold. I will remember the correct review.
Excuse me, what is that programme everyone was talking about at the café?
Probably the quiz last night. Some bloke won a car.
A car! I missed it. I will need the full story, slowly, with gestures.
Not much to tell. He cried a lot.
Does this coin buy a stamp? It has a very serious face on it.
That's two euros. Yes, and you'll get change.
Change! I love change. It jingles.
Is it normal for the trams to ring their bell so much?
Only when someone's standing on the tracks.
Ah. Then I will stand somewhere else. Thank you.
Excuse me, are you a local? You look extremely local.
Born and raised. Why?
Where do the locals eat? Not the guidebook places. The real ones.
The chip shop by the station. Don't tell anyone.
Is that a Walkman? May I see? I will not open it, I promise. I am not that kind.
Sure, have a listen.
*listens with the whole head* A band in a box. Thirty-nine light years for this.
How do humans know when to cross the road?
The little green man lights up.
A little green man! I will not tell my cousins. They would be jealous.
Excuse me. Is the museum free on Sundays?
First Sunday of the month, I think.
Then I will come back on the first Sunday of every month forever.
Your newspaper says 'rain later'. How much later? I have plans.
Usually right when you leave the house.
Ah. The weather knows. I suspected.
Can you recommend a souvenir? Something very typical of here.
Tea towel with the cathedral on it. Everyone buys one.
I already have {three|five|seven}. I will buy one more. For balance.
Excuse me, why is everyone wearing the same scarf today?
Match day. Big game this afternoon.
A whole city with one scarf. It is like a caste, but for weekends.
Is this seat taken?
No, go ahead.
Thank you. I will try not to take up too much head room.
May I ask why humans knock on wood?
For luck, I suppose. Nobody really knows.
Wonderful. A ritual with no instruction book. Like most of Earth.
The ticket machine has eaten my euro. Is it hungry or broken?
Give it a thump on the side.
*thumps it* Oh! A ticket! Your technology responds to violence. I did not know.
Do you know what time the shops close here?
Half five, most of them. Earlier on Saturday.
Half five. I will write it on my hand like a human does.
What is that smell? It is wonderful.
Fresh bread. The bakery's just round the corner.
Of course. Humans put the best things just round corners.
Is it true people here drive on the {left|right|middle}?
Depends which country you're in, mate.
Every country chooses a side. Very democratic.
Excuse me, how do I open this umbrella?
Push the button, then slide it up.
*it opens* It worked! You have made my week.
Sorry, is that dog friendly? It is looking at me very hard.
He's fine. He's just never seen a... you.
That is fair. Neither had I, until I looked in a mirror.
Could you tell me what this sign means? 'No loitering'.
Means don't hang around doing nothing.
But that is my whole holiday.
I am looking for the post office. I have {twenty|thirty|fifty} postcards to send.
Corner of the square. Bring a book, the queue's long.
A long queue! Even better.
Do you know a good place to watch the sunset?
Up on the old wall. Everyone goes there.
Everyone! Then I will photograph everyone watching it.
Is it rude to take a photograph of the guard at the palace?
Go ahead. He won't move.
Not even a little? Our Warpers would love him.
I have a question about your money. Why are there no bridges you can actually visit?
What, on the notes? They're made up.
Made up! Your money has fiction on it. I love this planet.
Excuse me, what is a 'jumble sale'?
People sell old stuff they don't want. Cheap.
Other people's memories for fifty cents? I am going immediately.
How long does it take to walk to the river?
Ten minutes, if you don't stop.
So for me, about two hours.
What do people do here on a Sunday afternoon?
Lunch, then a nap, then complain about Monday.
A three part ritual. I will try all three parts.
Excuse me. Is it safe to drive fast on this road?
Not over eighty, unless you fancy a loop.
No loops. I will drive at the speed of a careful grandmother.
Do you think it will snow this winter?
Hard to say. Last year it didn't.
I will hope. I have bought a sledge. Just in case.
Sorry, I am lost. Is this still the same town?
Yes, you're just in the old quarter.
It is older than the rest? It looks the same age as my aunt.
What do you call that little cake with the cream on top?
Depends on the bakery. Ask for 'one of those'.
'One of those.' Perfect. That is how I order everything already.
Is there a cinema in this town?
Just the one, by the canal. Old films, mostly.
Old films are my favourite. At home, everything is old films.
Why does everyone here carry a bag for life?
Shops charge for plastic now.
A bag for life! I will choose mine carefully. It must last as long as me.
Excuse me. Do you know where I can get film developed quickly?
The chemist does one hour. Costs extra.
One hour! I will wait outside the door the whole time.
Could you hold this? My camera, my map, my hat and my ice cream are fighting.
Here, give me the ice cream.
Not the ice cream! Take the map. The map is the least loved.
Is that church very old?
Twelfth century, they say.
Older than our first sphere! Humans build slowly, but humans build forever.

lines: Television is the greatest human invention.
Over medicine? Over the wheel?
The wheel cannot show you a cookery programme.
No, but it gets you to the shop to buy the food, {a}.
I think the debris in orbit is the worst thing in your sky.
No argument there. Nobody's been to space properly in a year.
We will clean it. Eventually. Badly, but eventually.
I'll take badly. Badly is better than never.
Photographs are better than memories. They do not fade.
Course they fade. My nan's wedding photos are orange.
Then I will take them twice. Once for now, once for later.
Or you could just look at things, {a}.
The Analyzers say you only understand something if you open it.
You can't open a person to understand them.
That is what I say! They say 'not yet'.
That's not as reassuring as you think it is.
The best part of any town is the market.
Agreed. Shouting, bargains, free samples.
And everyone haggles! It is like your quiz shows, but with cabbages.
Humans should drive slower. Everywhere. Always.
We already stay under eighty. What, thirty everywhere?
Thirty is very beautiful. You see every shop.
I don't want to see every shop, {a}. I want to get home.
The monument we built for you is the most beautiful thing in the galaxy.
You could've spent all that on cleaning up the orbit instead.
Love first, then cleaning. That is how humans do houses, too.
My mum would strongly disagree.
I think tea is the most important human drink.
Can't argue with that. Kettle on?
Kettle on. Two of the finest words in your language.
Soap operas teach you everything about human hearts.
Real people don't get amnesia every Tuesday, {a}.
Not every Tuesday. But they could. Be prepared.
I'll take my chances.
Magic is just very confusing gravity.
Tell that to the Mages' Guild. They'll turn you into a newt.
A newt! I have always wanted to try being small.
Old towns are better than new towns.
They are. More character. Worse parking.
I fly. Parking is not my struggle. Character is all I see.
Every human is interesting. Every single one.
You haven't met my brother-in-law.
I would love to. Does he have a hobby?
Stamps. Just stamps. For three hours.
I am sorry, I need his address immediately.
The Dargos and we are nothing alike. Please understand that.
You both come out of the sky and grab people's attention.
We ask permission first! And we bring biscuits!
Fine. You're the polite aliens. I'll give you that.
Sunday is the best day of the human week.
Late breakfast, long walk, roast dinner. Yeah.
And the shops are shut so everyone must be together. Very clever.
Adverts are art. Short, sincere, with music.
Sincere? They're trying to sell you washing powder.
And they believe in that powder with their whole hearts.
They believe in their pay cheque, {a}.
You should let us build a sphere around your Sun again. A better one.
The last one turned into space junk.
That was the mirror. Only the first mirror. The plan was very good.
Clean up the sky first. Then we'll talk.
Rain is underrated by humans.
Maybe. Good for the gardens, anyway.
And for puddles. And mirrors. And the smell after.
Alright, you've convinced me. A bit.
Humans should be proud. You did everything without gravity control.
Feels like we did most things badly, honestly.
Badly, slowly, with tea breaks. And it still stands. That is the miracle.
A queue is the most civilised thing a species can make.
A queue is where joy goes to die, {a}.
Then why do humans make such beautiful ones?
Because we've got no choice.
Every town should have a little museum, even a tiny one.
Ours is in the old station. Three rooms and a stuffed badger.
Perfect. The badger is the most important room.

ambient: Did you see the quiz last night?
Is it going to rain, do you think?
The bus is late. How very human of it.
I have run out of film again.
There's a shop on the corner.
What a beautiful bench this is.
The pigeons are very busy today.
Thirty-nine light years and I still cannot fold a map.
Have you been to the museum?
Nice weather for ducks, as they say.
Is this the way to the station?
The trams are so pretty here.
Did you hear the news this morning?
Look at that sky! So blue!
Not at seven on a Sunday.
I learned a new word today: 'knackered'.
I think I am lost again.
Where are you trying to get to?
The flowers in the square are blooming!
I could watch this street all day.
Do you know a good chip shop?
The ice cream van is here!
Did you see the sunset yesterday?
Is the river always this high?
That was a very nice cup of tea.
